(default 30). No CommandTimeout in stage-2 code (git grep).

MailKit Timeout "in milliseconds" (MailService.cs); StackExchange.Redis connectTimeout/syncTimeout/asyncTimeout "(ms)" (seredis.dev/Configuration); Npgsql Timeout/Command Timeout "(in seconds)" (connection-string-parameters). Names, counts and units differ per library as claimed; round-2 section-3 definition ("often more than one") matches.

Supported as a generalisation: Npgsql Command Timeout "Set to zero for infinity." (a client can wait without end); MailKit SmtpClient.cs @ 4.18.0 "int timeout = 2 * 60 * 1000;" (the library default is the lower-level limit). Round 2: section 4 now names both lower levels and says neither can be counted on to be short; the contradicting section-7 sentence was replaced (claim 20).

Trade-off stated with both sides and grounded in the code: sequential await in SendDueAsync (stage-2 lines 54-57) makes each stuck send's wait add to every later row; a timeout below a call's normal answer time fails that call by construction.

Definitional: a default is by definition what applies when the app sets nothing, and a library ships one value for all its users; that its documentation gives the value is shown for all three libraries by claims 11-13. No version-dependent behaviour asserted.

Docker API docs: "Use the cgroups freezer to suspend all processes in a container." MailKit @ 4.18.0 bounds connect (SocketUtils.ConnectAsync(..., Timeout, ...)) and each read (ReadAsync throws TimeoutException after ReadTimeout), so a paused Mailpit makes each attempt throw after about 10 s; NotificationSender.cs lines 77-80 route it to RecordFailure. A stopped container runs no process to accept or hold the connection, so step 1 fails without a timeout. Not executed.

SmtpClient.cs @ 4.18.0: "int timeout = 2 * 60 * 1000;"; Connect(string host, ...): "stream.WriteTimeout = timeout;" "stream.ReadTimeout = timeout;". With no Timeout line the default (2 min) still ends each connect/read, only later.
